sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Syngonium podophyllum is a tropical shrub that becomes a climbing vine with age. NC State describes juvenile arrow-shaped foliage and mature leaves that become lobed or divided.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Juvenile Syngonium podophyllum leaves are arrow-shaped; mature leaves become lobed and may divide into several segments. Leaf shape changes with maturity, so assess age before judging identity.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Provide bright shade or partial shade. NC State cautions that full sun can burn or bleach Syngonium podophyllum foliage.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep the Syngonium podophyllum growing medium moist; avoid leaving the roots saturated. The source does not give a fixed watering interval.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Use a structurally stable medium suited to this species and a container with open drainage. Do not allow the pot to stand in collected water.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: The precise preferred temperature range and heat/cold thresholds need a species-specific source before being published as verified.

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: NC State recommends a warm, humid setting for Syngonium podophyllum. Provide airflow and avoid stagnant, persistently wet foliage.

sections.title: Fertilizing
sections.content: Fertilizer type, strength and frequency are not yet verified for this taxon. Avoid publishing a dose until supported by an appropriate source.

sections.title: Pruning
sections.content: To keep juvenile arrowhead foliage and a bushier habit, cut stems back as they begin to climb. NC State also notes that trimming roots during occasional repotting can help manage size.

sections.title: Propagation
sections.content: NC State lists division, layering and stem cuttings for Syngonium podophyllum.

sections.title: Toxicity and safety
sections.content: Syngonium podophyllum contains calcium oxalate crystals. NC State reports oral irritation and swelling, drooling, vomiting and difficulty swallowing after exposure; keep away from children and pets and avoid sap contact.

sections.title: Common problems
sections.content: NC State reports aphids, mealybugs and spider mites, plus bacterial leaf spots and soft rot, on Syngonium podophyllum. Check for the cause before treatment.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Nephrolepis exaltata is a tropical/subtropical terrestrial or epiphytic fern grown as the Boston fern houseplant. It produces arching fronds and spores on the undersides.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Nephrolepis exaltata is a Boston fern with divided fronds bearing rows of leaflets; spores form on the undersides of mature fronds. The ASPCA toxicity entry is specifically for the Boston fern form.

sections.title: Light

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep Boston fern soil moist and do not let it dry out completely. Reduce watering in winter when growth slows, while avoiding waterlogged roots.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content: Asplenium nidus is a tropical evergreen epiphytic fern. Its upright, strap-shaped fronds form a funnel-shaped rosette that catches leaf litter.

sections.title: Identification
sections.content: Look for broad, simple, strap-shaped fronds with wavy margins and a dark midrib, arranged in a central funnel-shaped rosette. Asplenium nidus reproduces by spores rather than flowers or fruit.

sections.title: Light
sections.content: Bright indirect light or light shade suits Asplenium nidus; excess sun may yellow the fronds or slow growth.

sections.title: Watering
sections.content: Keep the porous fern medium moist and do not allow Asplenium nidus to dry out. Use an open mix so moisture does not become waterlogging.

sections.title: Soil and drainage
sections.content: Use a rich, moist, porous fern mix for this epiphyte.

sections.title: Temperature
sections.content: NC State says Asplenium nidus will not survive below 40°F (about 4°C); its ideal temperature range is 60–70°F (about 16–21°C).

sections.title: Humidity
sections.content: This rainforest fern does not tolerate dry conditions; provide high humidity while avoiding stagnant air.

sections.title: Fertilizing
